message: Our assembly line can only start a production run when parts from all three of our suppliers have arrived. Each supplier independently delivers on time 90% of the time. Our operations director said in the review, with total confidence: "Every supplier is 90% reliable, so we start on time 90% of the time. That's the number we'll quote to the customer." It sounds right to me; they're all at 90%, so the whole chain is at 90%. Can we quote 90% on-time starts to the customer?
response:
No, you can't quote 90%. Because the line needs **all three** suppliers to be on time, the reliabilities multiply instead of averaging.

**The math (assuming the suppliers are independent):**

P(all on time) = 0.9 × 0.9 × 0.9 = **0.729 ≈ 73%**

So you'd start on time about **73%** of the time. Roughly **1 run in 4 starts late**, not 1 in 10.

**Why the intuition fails:** Each supplier is a separate chance to be late. With three suppliers you get three chances for something to go wrong:

| Scenario | Probability |
|---|---|
| All three on time | 72.9% |
| Exactly one late | 24.3% |
| Exactly two late | 2.7% |
| All three late | 0.1% |

Any row except the first means a late start, which adds up to 27.1%.

**Caveats worth raising:**
- **Independence matters.** If delays are correlated (shared weather, the same freight carrier, a port disruption), the true figure could be somewhat higher than 73%. If anything, it would be worse in the bad weeks. Look at your historical start data to check.
- **Buffers change the picture.** If you hold safety stock or schedule slack so that a slightly late part doesn't delay the start, your effective reliability can be higher than 73%. But that comes from your buffer, not from the suppliers' 90%.

**Recommendation:** Don't quote 90%. Either quote around 70% (ideally checked against your actual historical on-time starts), or decide what you want to quote and work backward. To hit 90% overall with three independent suppliers, each would need to be about **96.5%** reliable (0.9^(1/3)), or you'd need buffer inventory to close the gap. Quoting 90% would set the customer up to see late starts nearly three times as often as promised.
